Comprehensive Guide to Making Homemade Sourdough Bread
————————————————————————————
CONTENTS
1. Introduction
2. Equipment Checklist
3. Understanding Your Starter
4. Ingredients & Baker’s Percentages
5. The Timeline at a Glance
6. Step-by-Step Process
   A. Feeding the Starter
   B. Autolyse
   C. Mixing & Gluten Development
   D. Bulk Fermentation
   E. Pre-Shape & Bench Rest
   F. Final Shape & Proof
   G. Scoring, Baking & Steaming
7. Common Problems & Fixes
8. Flavor Variations & Add-Ins
9. Storing & Reviving Bread
10. Frequently Asked Questions
————————————————————————————

1. INTRODUCTION
Sourdough is bread leavened naturally with a culture of wild yeast and lactic-acid bacteria. It yields superior flavor, keeps longer, and requires only flour, water, and salt. Mastering it demands patience, observation, and a few repetitions, but it’s approachable for any home baker.

2. EQUIPMENT CHECKLIST
• Kitchen scale (indispensable)  
• Mixing bowl(s)  
• Dough scraper / bench knife  
• Proofing basket or colander lined with a floured towel  
• Dutch oven or baking stone + steam apparatus (e.g., cast-iron skillet with hot water)  
• Razor blade / lame for scoring  
• Thermometer (ambient & dough)  
• Clean countertop space  
• Plastic wrap or reusable shower cap for covering dough  
Optional: stand mixer (dough hook), rice flour for dusting, banneton, digital timer/app.

3. UNDERSTANDING YOUR STARTER
A starter is a mixture of flour and water that’s been colonized by wild microorganisms. Mature starter is bubbly, doubles in size 4-8 h after feeding, smells pleasantly tangy, and passes the “float test” (a spoonful floats in water).

Maintenance schedule (100 % hydration example):  
Daily (room temp) – Discard all but 50 g, feed with 50 g water + 50 g flour.  
Refrigerated (weekly) – Same ratio, but store in fridge after feeding; remove and reactivate 1–2 feeds before baking.

4. INGREDIENTS & BAKER’S PERCENTAGES (yields 1 large or 2 small boules)
• Bread flour: 450 g (90 %)  
• Whole-wheat flour: 50 g (10 %)  
• Water: 350 g (70 %) + 20 g for bassinage (4 %)  
• Mature starter (100 % hydration): 100 g (20 %)  
• Salt: 10 g (2 %)

Feel free to push hydration up to 78 % once comfortable; more water = more open crumb.

5. TIMELINE AT A GLANCE (room temp 22 °C / 72 °F)
Day 1  
08:00 Feed starter  
12:00 Mix autolyse  
12:30 Add starter & salt, begin folds  
12:30–17:00 Bulk fermentation (4.5 h, folds every 30 min first 2 h)  
17:00 Pre-shape, 20 min bench rest  
17:30 Final shape, into banneton  
17:40 Cold proof in fridge (12–48 h)

Day 2  
08:00–11:00 Preheat oven & bake directly from fridge

6. STEP-BY-STEP PROCESS

A. Feeding the Starter  
1. Discard down to 50 g starter.  
2. Add 50 g water (room temp) + 50 g flour (50 % bread, 50 % whole-wheat accelerates activity).  
3. Stir, mark level with rubber band, cover loosely. Use when doubled.

B. Autolyse (flour + water rest)  
1. Combine 500 g flour with 350 g water until no dry spots remain.  
2. Cover 30–60 min. Purpose: allows enzymes to hydrate flour, jump-starts gluten formation, improves extensibility.

C. Mixing & Gluten Development  
1. Sprinkle 10 g salt over dough. Add 100 g bubbly starter.  
2. Pinch and fold until incorporated; rest 15 min.  
3. Perform 1–2 “slap and folds” or use stand mixer on low 3–4 min until dough is smoother.  
4. Optional bassinage: add remaining 20 g water gradually while folding to reach final hydration.

D. Bulk Fermentation  
Goal: Dough rises 30–50 %, feels airy, domes on top, shows bubbles at edges.  
• Temperature control: Ideal dough temp 24–26 °C (75–78 °F).  
• Folding regime: Stretch & fold or coil fold every 30 min for first 2 h (4–5 folds). Each fold: lift, stretch gently, fold over itself, rotate bowl. Builds strength without kneading.  
• Total bulk 4–6 h depending on temp, flour strength, inoculation %.

E. Pre-Shape & Bench Rest  
1. Gently scrape dough onto unfloured counter.  
2. Using scraper, tighten into a round by dragging toward you until surface tension forms.  
3. Rest 15–30 min uncovered; dough relaxes for final shaping.

F. Final Shape & Proof  
Common shapes: boule (round) or bâtard (oval).  
Boule: Flip dough smooth side down, fold bottom third up, sides to center, top down, then roll into tight ball.  
Place seam-side up in a floured banneton (rice flour resists sticking).  
Proof options:  
• Room temp 1–2 h until dough slowly springs back when poked (finger dent test).  
• Cold proof 12–48 h at 4 °C / 39 °F for convenience and flavor; dough firms, easier to score.

G. Scoring, Baking & Steaming  
Preheat: 250 °C / 480 °F with Dutch oven inside 45 min-1 h.  
1. Turn loaf onto parchment or preheated peel, seam side down.  
2. Score 1 cm deep at 30–45° angle (e.g., single ear slash) to control expansion.  
3. Transfer to Dutch oven, cover lid. Bake 20 min with lid (steam).  
4. Remove lid, reduce to 230 °C / 445 °F, bake 20-25 min until deep brown, internal temp 96 °C / 205 °F.  
5. Cool on rack minimum 1 h before slicing; crumb sets, moisture redistributes.

7. COMMON PROBLEMS & FIXES
Dense loaf → Underproofed, weak starter; extend bulk/proof or refresh starter twice.  
Flat loaf → Overproofed; reduce bulk time or starter %; ensure shaping adds tension.  
Tight crumb → Low hydration, insufficient folds; increase water, improve gluten.  
Gummy interior → Cut too soon or under-baked; verify internal temp >95 °C.  
Pale crust → Insufficient caramelization; bake hotter or longer, remove lid earlier.  
Sticks to banneton → Lack of rice flour or over-proofed; use rice/AP flour mixture 50:50.

8. FLAVOR VARIATIONS & ADD-INS
• Seeds: 15 % toasted sunflower, pumpkin, flax; soak (“soaker”) equal weight water to keep dough hydrated.  
• Olives & Herbs: 20 % chopped olives, 2 % rosemary, fold in during last coil fold.  
• Whole-grain boost: Replace up to 40 % with rye/spelt; adjust water +5-10 %.  
• Sweet: Swirl in cinnamon sugar and raisins during shaping; beware of sugar slowing fermentation.

9. STORING & REVIVING BREAD
Short-term: Keep cut-side down on board, covered with linen 24 h.  
Medium: Paper bag inside plastic bag at room temp 3-4 d.  
Freeze: Slice, bag airtight, freeze up to 3 mo; reheat 200 °C 10 min or toast from frozen.  
Reviving crust: Splash loaf with water, bake 180 °C 10 min.

10. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Q: Can I use whole-grain starter in white bread?  
A: Yes; flavor and activity often improve.

Q: How do I adapt to warmer climate?  
A: Lower starter % (e.g., 10 %) or bulk in cooler spot 22 °C; refrigerate dough earlier.

Q: Why score right before baking?  
A: Maximum gas retention; cold dough from fridge is easiest to slash cleanly.

Q: Can I bake without Dutch oven?  
A: Yes; bake on stone/steel, add steam via pan with boiling water 15 min, then vent.

Q: How do I scale recipe?  
A: Multiply ingredient grams; keep baker’s percentages consistent.

—Happy baking!
